section.title: Purpose
section.text: N-17 is where an LLM turns one anchor of this spec book into a set of small tickets as data. It replaces the architect as the hub for every cut, which the owner halted for overload on 2026-10-14T00:38Z (rebuild/investigation/03-DECISIONS.md#18-d16-may-an-llm-decompose-work-into-tickets option A), and it replaces the approval stamp (238 of 238 approvals were overrides, L11 F3) with a validator that runs the acceptance on main before any ticket exists (N-18).

A spec-author never authors a design and never edits the repository: the design is this book (D14), the output is a draft record in the store (D04), and the architect reads nothing until check.sh passes (brief C, Seats). The owner's rule is that tickets are small, one concern each, a few files, a diff a reviewer reads in minutes; when in doubt split (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md design first).

section.title: Input: the spec-author brief inside a seat run
section.text: The dispatch's target names anchor (a pointer into this book, for example rebuild/design/nodes/N-14/spec.xml#mechanism, or a node id for the whole node), group, the cut request (its id, source record and, for a fix, the rejected id and hold id) when the key is CR-..., and on a retry verdict_ref (the validator.refused record). N-13 renders bundle_dir/brief.md with:
section.field: the section or volume the anchor points to, copied verbatim from the repository at repo_sha, plus its checklist section, because every ticket's acceptance must map to a checklist item's proof.
every ticket record in the store cut from the same anchor (id, title, status, files), so the draft extends rather than duplicates.

one concern per ticket; files declared and disjoint inside the set; acceptance commands that run from the repository root through make targets or scripts in the repository; input and output records declared from the node's record.schema.json; depends_on by key inside the set or by id outside; a ticket touching an owner surface names its screenshot proof (memory screenshot-every-page-change); a ticket that flips a node live is separate from the ticket that builds it dark (build-mode rule).
on a retry: the validator.refused record verbatim, with the failing command, its observed exit and stderr tail, or the check that failed (overlap, cycle, size).
ticket-set.draft shape, section ticket-shape; limits stated once.
section.text: The workspace is read-only, detached at origin/main (N-14 mode read-only); the spec-author reads code to size tickets and name real paths and real make targets.

section.title: Output record: ticket-set.draft
section.text: Kind ticket-set.draft, code 100, written by the launcher's post step from the validated structured output. Fields: set_id (equals run_id), anchor, group, attempt, author_session_id, tickets (an array, section ticket-shape), rationale (one paragraph on the split), verdict_ref (on a retry). idempotency_key = run_id. A draft is never a ticket: ticket ids are minted by N-18 on acceptance, so a refused draft leaves nothing behind but its record.

A blocked output (the anchor is contradictory, or already fully ticketed, or needs a ruling) is seat.result 423 seat_blocked with observations naming the anchor lines; "needs a ruling" carries a proposed card (about, decide, options) that N-28 can post as is.

section.title: Mechanism: the brief, the run, the draft put by code
section.mermaid: flowchart LR A[dispatch target: anchor, group, verdict_ref] --> B[N-13 brief: anchor text, checklist, existing tickets, rules, verdict] B --> R[claude -p run on the role's model, read-only workspace] R --> O{structured output ticket-set.draft} O -- tickets --> P[launcher post step: shape check, put ticket-set.draft 100] O -- blocked --> X[seat.result 423 with observations or a proposed card] P --> V[N-18 validator]
section.step: The run: the spec-author reads the anchor and the checklist, reads the code the anchor names, and writes tickets as data in the output schema. It makes no file change: Write and Edit are denied; its Bash is read-only (git log|show|grep, rg, ls, make lint to learn the target names). It may run no acceptance command itself: N-18 does, on main, and records the observed exit; a spec-author that runs a command is guessing at what the validator will see.

The post step (scheduler/internal/launcher/specauthor.go): validate the structured output against record.schema.json (the launcher already did; this is the second, same check before a put), add set_id, anchor, group, attempt, author_session_id, put ticket-set.draft with idempotency_key run_id. No mint, no file, no pull request.
N-18 starts on the committed draft (level-triggered). The spec-author is gone by then.
section.text: Model: roles/spec-author.json model.claude (claude-opus-5-5 today; the right-size rule allows Sonnet by a ruling); effort high; limits from seats.json spec-author: max_turns 150, budget 25 USD, wall clock 3600 s, stall 600 s.

section.title: The ticket as data: what every drafted ticket declares
section.field: t1..tn inside the set; the validator mints the id.
the full title; the pull request title will be "<id> - <title>".
the node id and anchor the ticket builds; a ticket builds one node.
one sentence; a ticket with two concerns is refused by the validator's size check and by the reviewer's judgement.
declared paths or globs, bash glob rule of factory/bin/claims.sh; at most seats.json ticket_max_files (default 6); never an aggregate or a runtime path; disjoint across the set.

the record kind that starts the work and the record kind that proves it, from the node's record.schema.json; for a dark build the output is the test proof; for a go-live ticket the output is the first real record of the node.

one or more commands with runs_in (host or pod), expect_exit after the change (0 for a test, or a named non-zero for a refusal test), and the checklist item each proves. The validator records observed_exit_on_main.
keys inside the set or ticket ids outside; acyclic.
worker (default) or spec-author (a ticket whose files are specs or roles or this book's volumes).
files count and an estimated diff lines; a reviewer reads it in minutes (owner: this is a factory not a slog fest).
for an owner-surface ticket, the screenshot path pattern under the state root; for a go-live ticket, the named proof the build-mode rule requires.
numbered, short, with the degrees of freedom named.
section.text: Schema: record.schema.json#/$defs/draft_ticket.

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.text: A spec-author dispatch is created by N-07 from a spec-phase lease on a cut-request key (CR-<request id>), which N-02 grants on the ticket.ready N-03 writes when it admits a ticket.request record (writers: N-10 a fix for a held main, N-30 rule R05 a cut: message, N-49 a LAND row, N-50 the archive ticket; nodes/N-03/spec.xml#input), or from a validator.refused that N-11 turns into attempt n+1 on the same cut-request key. The go-live tickets of the cut-over order (shared/cut-over.xml#order) are briefed one per step in that order; before the scheduler goes live (shared/cut-over.xml#step-usergo) the rebuild plan's seats run those briefs under build mode (shared/cut-over.xml#builders), after it N-07 dispatches them like any other cut request. The run is an N-15 process; the brief is its argument. No architect cuts, approves, or types; the architect reads the book once it passes check.sh and rules only through cards.

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.timeout: wall clock 3600 s, stall 600 s, max turns 150, budget 25 USD
wait.fallback: N-15 kills and records blocked; N-11 counts the attempt
phase.failed 500; the recovery pass re-puts from result.json (idempotent by run_id)

wait.timeout: not waited on by this node; the seat is gone
wait.fallback: N-18 has its own bounds; a draft with no validator record after N-18's bound is N-18's failure record

section.title: Retries up to 3, then recover and report
section.text: A validator.refused is a failure record; N-11 dispatches attempt n+1 with verdict_ref and a fresh session (a refused cut is re-thought, not resumed); after attempt 3 the anchor is dead for cutting and N-28 posts one card with the three refusals, whose options are: the architect's ruling on the anchor (a card), a change to the volume (a spec-author ticket on the book itself), or cancel. A seat.result blocked (limits, crash) retries the same way. The post step's put retries 3 times then phase.failed; recovery is the level-triggered pass of N-15.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.text: Many spec-authors run at once, one per anchor (the seven groups of ../../dag.md#5-groups-for-parallel-authors were written exactly this way); none writes a file, so there is no file to collide on. Each draft is its own record keyed by run_id.

Collision 1, two drafts for one anchor (a retry overlapping a late first run, or two cut requests): both drafts are committed; N-18 validates both; the second's tickets that duplicate the first's (same node, same files) are refused by the validator's overlap check against accepted tickets, so one set of tickets exists. The brief's existing tickets list makes the second author see the first's accepted tickets when they are already in the store.

Collision 2, drafts from two anchors declare overlapping files: both are valid drafts; N-18 accepts both (files overlap across sets is a scheduling order, not a cut defect); N-03 serializes their readiness by the claims rule.

Collision 3, the anchor volume changes on main while a spec-author reads it: the brief carries the text at repo_sha; the draft names repo_sha; the validator refuses a draft whose repo_sha is older than the anchor's last change on main with reason anchor_moved, and attempt n+1 reads the new text.

Collision 4, the owner cuts a ticket by hand through a card: it enters as a cut request with the owner's words as the anchor; it still goes through a spec-author run and the validator, so a hand cut is never an unvalidated ticket.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.code: A draft exists. Acts: N-18 only.

Blocked: seat_blocked (anchor contradictory, fully ticketed, needs a ruling with a proposed card), or any launcher reason. Acts: N-11; a needs-a-ruling block with a proposed card goes to N-28 as that card after the first attempt, not the third, because retrying a question is nagging.
The draft put failed 3 times. Acts: the recovery pass, then N-11.

path.writes: result.json holds the draft as returned; transcript.jsonl
path.retention: 7 days; 30 days when the anchor died

section.text: Drafts live in the store (table ticket_sets, kept for the life of the anchor's tickets; pruned by N-45's store retention when every ticket of the set is merged or cancelled plus 30 days). Nothing is written into the repository: a cut is not a pull request (D04 option C ends cut PRs).

section.title: Permissions
section.text: The spec-author seat (from N-13): Read, Grep, Glob, Bash read-only (git log|show|grep|ls-files, rg, ls, cat, make -n, make lint); denied: Write, Edit, Agent, Task, git push, gh *, podman *, any make target that changes files, any path under $COQ_STATE except its own brief. Model from roles/spec-author.json.
The post step (code): gRPC put only.

section.title: Monitoring
section.text: Counters: drafts_written, drafts_refused (from N-18, by check), tickets_per_draft histogram, files_per_ticket histogram, spec_author_cost_usd, needs_ruling_cards. The Stats screen (N-40) shows tickets cut per hour and the refusal rate by check; a refusal rate above seats.json draft_refusal_alert (default 0.5 over the last 10 drafts) is an alert on N-41 because the brief template or the anchor is at fault, not the seats.

section.title: Runbook
section.text: See a draft: scheduler status lists ticket sets with set_id, anchor, attempt, verdict; the draft body is result.json in the run directory and the record in the store.

An anchor dead after three refusals: the card names the three checks that failed; the usual fix is the volume (the acceptance it asks for cannot run on main) and the ticket for that is a spec-author ticket on rebuild/design, which goes through the same path.

Cut a ticket by hand: not a path; the owner's words on a card become a cut request record (N-29) and a spec-author run drafts it. The break glass (N-42) can dispatch that run outside the tick; it cannot skip the validator.
Cleanup: run directories by cleanup-seat-runs.sh; store retention of ticket_sets by N-45.
